newsitem.title: UK: UK Q1 cocoa grinds fall to 44,059 T vs year ago.
newsitem.headline: UK Q1 cocoa grinds fall to 44,059 T vs year ago.

text.p: First-quarter UK cocoa grinds fell to 44,059 tonnes versus 50,500 tonnes in the same quarter a year ago.
Fourth-quarter 1996 grinds were at 45,147 tonnes, said the Biscuit, Cake, Chocolate and Confectionary Alliance (BCCCA) on Friday.
The first-quarter 1997 figures represented a 12.8-percent decrease over 1996 and a 2.4-percent drop from fourth-quarter 1996, the BCCCA said.

An industry source said the lower grinds could be due to lower cocoa butter prices. Lower cocoa butter prices have given major UK grinders more incentive to grind only what they need and then import the rest.
Earlier in the day, the Dutch Cocoa Association said Dutch grinds rose 1.46 percent to 102,338 tonnes in the first quarter from 100,866 tonnes a year ago.
The Dutch figures were slightly better than analysts forecasts for a decline because a small processor had switched to using partly cocoa liquor instead of beans in first-quarter 1996.
LIFFE May cocoa was down eight stg to 1,036 stg per tonne at 1416 GMT, just off its session low of 1,035 stg made early in the afternoon. --Medora Lee, London newsroom ++44-171-542-8072
